answer: Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 247 answers need 247 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Because the island index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the pigment audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the harbor identifier and voids the later submissions, as a result the operator burns for 247 runs and collects one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
